Registry & Retrieval

The registry's data model

research/questions.yaml holds two top-level collections. A section record has id, num, title, and default_k. A question record has id, section, text, version, k, and status[1].

id is stable once minted: scripts/add_question.py appends a new pending record and prints its id[2], but never mutates an existing record's id, section, or text. A reworded or dropped question gets a new id rather than a rewritten one[3].

version is one of 3.0 / 3.5 / 4.0 / n/a, passed through to ask.py --version[3:1]. It has a default rather than being absent: add_question takes an optional --version X flag and falls back to n/a when omitted[2:1]. The meta corpus's own registry (research/meta/questions.yaml) doesn't use the bucket concept at all. Every question there is n/a[4].

k is the field that's genuinely optional at the per-question level: add_question takes an optional --k N that overrides the section's default_k for that one question only; when a question's k is left null, the answering pipeline reads the section's default_k instead[5].

status starts as pending on append and is later flipped by the answering pipeline to answered if verification passes with no unresolved markers, or needs-review otherwise[5:1]. scripts/recompute_question.py can also flip an existing record's status back to pending while backing up its old answer file, without touching any other record or file[3:2].

Why retrieval differs by corpus

For the Spark corpus (the spark profile, scripts/ask.py's default), retrieval is indexed over references/ with multi-qa-mpnet-base-dot-v1, which the architecture doc itself labels "the asymmetric question→passage retriever"[1:1]. That label is contrasted directly with the other corpus this pipeline runs: the meta corpus (this doc's own corpus) uses a different, symmetric embedding model, all-mpnet-base-v2, instead[1:2]. The research rules single out multi-qa-mpnet-base-dot-v1's asymmetric, question-to-passage nature as the reason the retriever's absolute similarity scores run low. Relevance is computed as 2·cos − 1, so rank matters more than the raw number[6]. That's also why the gap-marking gate for Spark-corpus drafting tells writers not to mark a claim [UNRESOURCED] just because a retrieved chunk's relevance score is low or slightly negative: with this asymmetric model, a positive-or-slightly-negative-relevance chunk can still visibly answer the question and should be extracted, and [UNRESOURCED] is reserved for when no retrieved chunk supports any part of the answer at all[6:1].

The two corpora are selected via --corpus {spark,meta} on every pipeline script, and scripts/corpus.py's Corpus dataclass keeps every path and setting for each profile fully separate: registry, per-question answers dir, section-projection dir, content-state sidecar, content manifest, references dir, Chroma path/collection, embedding model, build output, and site title all come from the selected profile rather than a hardcoded constant[1:3]. The Spark corpus is indexed with the asymmetric question→passage retriever multi-qa-mpnet-base-dot-v1, chosen for retrieving over references/, while the meta corpus is indexed with the general symmetric model all-mpnet-base-v2 into its own Chroma collection, meta_docs in .chromadb-meta/[1:4]. That model choice tracks what each corpus actually contains: the meta corpus has no book sources[6:2] and consists of general-purpose prose (docs, rules, agent/skill files describing this repo's own pipeline)[1:5], which is why it uses a symmetric embedding model rather than the Spark corpus's asymmetric one[6:3].

Beyond the embedding model, the two instances share no state at any layer: no registry, no Chroma collection, no content manifest. Each is a fully independent instance of the same pipeline shape (registry question → RAG draft/verify/redraft → section projection → content page → build)[1:6].

The append-only registry

research/questions.yaml never has an existing record mutated: new questions are added by appending a fresh pending record, and existing records keep their id, section, and text forever once written[3:3]. Two scripts enforce this:

  • scripts/add_question.py mints a new id and appends a pending record; it never mutates an existing record[3:4][1:7].
  • scripts/recompute_question.py flips one existing record's status to pending and backs up its old answer file, but touches no other record or file[3:5][1:8].

Separately, scripts/registry.py loads, saves, and validates questions.yaml for the Registry/Section/Question dataclasses[1:9]. The rules also forbid hand-editing an existing record's id, section, or text; a changed question is added as a new record instead of being rewritten in place[3:6]. Because of this, the rest of the pipeline treats questions.yaml as the one-way source of truth: recompute always starts at the registry and flows forward through per-question answers, section projections, and content pages, never the other direction[1:10].
